NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION:

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks inverter output power and efficiency, and triggers on absolute temperature thresholds.
Our observable is the normalized harmonic distortion in the AC output current, specifically the 3rd harmonic component relative to the fundamental frequency, which increases as IGBT degradation causes switching irregularities and capacitor degradation causes filtering inefficiency.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
This observable is computable from the existing AC current measurement using standard FFT analysis, which is a basic engineering function available in most industrial control systems.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks aggregate power output and absolute temperature thresholds, which only react after failure has occurred. Our observable is the normalized 3rd harmonic distortion in AC current, which increases as IGBT degradation causes switching irregularities and capacitor degradation reduces filtering effectiveness, providing early detection of semiconductor and component degradation before thermal runaway occurs.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing physical relation is that IGBT switching irregularities introduce odd harmonics into the output current, with the 3rd harmonic being most prominent due to three-phase system characteristics. As degradation progresses, switching times increase, raising harmonic content. The magnitude verification: a healthy inverter should have THD < 3% with 3rd harmonic < 0.5% of fundamental. Degradation increases 3rd harmonic to >1.5% of fundamental before thermal runaway occurs, representing a 3× increase from baseline.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
Components: Existing AC current sensors, existing data logging system, standard FFT analysis software
Materials: None additional
Instruments: Existing inverter telemetry system
Procedure: 
1. Collect 3-phase AC current data at 5-minute intervals
2. Perform FFT analysis on each phase
3. Calculate normalized 3rd harmonic magnitude (I3/I1) for each phase
4. Average the three phase values
5. Compare against threshold
All computation uses standard industrial control system functions - no specialized equipment required.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
Installability: SAME - uses existing sensors and data logging infrastructure
Operability: SAME - runs continuously in background, no additional operator intervention
Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance required over standard monitoring
Rough cost class: SAME - no additional hardware or software costs beyond standard monitoring
The approach imposes no additional deployment burden while providing earlier detection than standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Monitor 100 inverters in the field for 12 months, comparing the normalized 3rd harmonic indicator against actual failures.
Instruments: Existing inverter telemetry system
Pass/Fail threshold: Must detect at least 90% of failures at least 2 weeks before trip, with false positive rate ≤ 1 per quarter per inverter
Duration: 12 months
Kill criterion: If the false positive rate exceeds 1 per quarter per inverter, or if fewer than 90% of failures are detected at least 2 weeks before trip, the predictor is invalidated.
